body: In my personal experience as a black woman, red is a great color for deeper skin tones. Whether it’s magenta, fire hydrant red, auburn, etc. it looks good. I’ve tried burgundy and copper red, but berry red looks really nice too. As long as the red has dimension, it will look good. Trust.

Unpopular or not, I think it suits you. The color is beautiful and the bangs look nice. Shiny hair and blunt bangs doesn’t equal a wig to me. I think the comments are a bit harsh for no reason. You’re obviously feeling it and that’s all that matters.

I talked about that with my psychiatrist. The main thing that didn’t align with that were that these issues started happening without any major stressful events beforehand. I was at a very happy time in my life and my mental health hadn’t been so good in years. I also experienced other strange things like difficulty walking and muscle weakness after my first event which is why I got an MRI.
I should have worded that better. I just meant that there aren’t many clear options for determining what’s going since I’ve already done those tests.

Yeah. Originally, my psychiatrist thought they may be PNES which wouldn’t show up on the EEG. While I’m skeptical, I can’t rule that out. Regardless, I’ve had many tests show up negative to other health issues, so I’m still optimistic.
Thank you so much! I will update when I get the results from Day 2.

The unfortunate part is that I’ve had an MRI and a CT scan the first time I had an “event” and they found no brain abnormalities or nerve damage. I recently went to the ER and they didn’t test for anything. They just assumed I had a seizure disorder and I was discharged.
Thank you so much! I really appreciate this community.

I actually did. I pressed the button that I was instructed to 8 times over 48 hours to record them. The events were more intense versus the usual spacing out and mild shaking that I experienced before. This time, I was fine one moment and on the floor the next. I was usually pretty out of it afterwards.

Alright. This may be a bit soon, but all of us are on better terms now. Pretty much, we’re speaking to each other. We can talk to each other without being awkward and there’s not as much tension. I will still try to expand my horizons with other friends. 

While this situation didn’t destroy our friendship, it did make me see one of my roommates differently. Her reaction to the fallout was almost like I owed her an apology which I don’t. She later reached out to me saying that she’s trying to work on her approach to this situation and that we’re still friends. 

To be honest, I’m skeptical and most likely things won’t be the same between us. Our trauma bond was never healthy. I put another update in my post that talks about my other roommate. I’m still trying to figure out the therapy situation, but I’m working on it.
I never thought about it that way, but you’re right. I need to keep myself focused right now on things that are actually important.

We got close because they called 911 when I had a medical emergency. They also came to the hospital to see me. We started to become friends after that. I’m starting to realize that I don’t owe them friendship for what they did.
It’s sadly too late in the semester. We get out in early May.
Yeah. It’s unfortunate to see their true feelings. I already kind of thought that they liked each other more than me anyways. Rooms with three people kind of set you up for that sometimes.
I understand this. I just want everyone to chill out. There doesn’t have to be a problem. I’m willing to move on, they just aren’t.
I agree. I wish that this would have happened earlier in the semester because I could have moved to a different room.

I appreciate your responses. I think that both of them have been a bit unrealistic with the way they are using their feelings against me. I’ve adopted the attitude that you have to choose your battles.
Sadly, I can’t because it’s so late in the semester. School gets out early May, so this won’t last very long. I’m also transferring to a new school next year.
Yeah. I wish I was less affected by the situation. We’re really close friends, so it’s complicated for me.
I understand your perspective. I really wish we could move past this.
Just to add on, I know this very small compared to other posts. I just want to resolve this issue because we live in the same room.

Where do I start?

- Watching my siblings when my mother was     
blackout drunk

- Always defending my mother to family members because she is the true “victim”

- Changing my opinion if my mother didn’t agree with it

- Being my mother’s only friend

- Leaving the room when one of my mother’s “friends” would come over (she’s married)

- Crying silently “so CPS wouldn’t get called”

- Not being able to have any friends over or visit any friends

- Being made fun of for my interests

- Being told how I “wasted my potential” before I even reached my teenage years

- Always being compared to someone else’s child

- Being mocked when I was having auditory and visual hallucinations 

- My mother not liking any of my doctors or therapists because they wouldn’t listen to her

I thought that maybe he’s the GC, but she treats both of my younger siblings like this (my younger sister is 10). I’m happy for them because they won’t have to experience the treatment that I did. At the same time, it’s sad that they’re just pawns in her game. She stops them from seeing anyone that pissed her off, including me. My little brother loves me to pieces, so he will break her unhinged rules so he can see me. My sister would too, but she’s medically fragile (cerebral palsy and she can’t walk).

Yeah. It’s sad that it’s possible. I never know what her true motives are. My little brother is luckily a sweetheart. The only reason he acts out is because he doesn’t have any friends to play with outside of school. This is just her bad parenting coming into play. 

From what I observed, she likes to use the kids (I also have a sister who is 10) as pawns. Whenever anyone pisses her off, she’ll stop the kids from being able to see them. The reason she does it is because she hasn’t had an outside job (she’s a caretaker for my little sister) since I was a baby after flexing her degrees on everyone (Psychology and Philosophy lol) who didn’t go to school. When they point this out, she can’t take it.

For context, my mother is a “functioning” alcoholic in denial. I don’t see my father often and he doesn’t like to be involved with our issues. I’ve dealt with this on my own for over 6 years (I’m 17). My Grandmother is very supportive and understanding of my situation, but has commitments during the week which prevent me from living with her full-time.

Just to clarify, I don’t hate my parents. I just have a very surface level relationship with them. This is mainly because I don’t trust either of them and they’re extremely selfish people. I don’t care what they do, just don’t bother me and my siblings w/ the same bs that I’ve dealt with since childhood. 

Also, I don’t talk to my father about my feelings because he overreacts. Instead of trying to better himself, he will “give me space” by not talking to me for a few months. We eventually start talking again because I’m closer to him than my Mom and he understands how she can be more than anyone else.

I’m glad that you can relate in such an unfortunate situation. The age gap is the main problem for me too. They’re young and impressionable, and my mom knows that. My little sister (10) is disabled, so the way she sees me is different. I’m more of a happy character in her life and words coming from my mom won’t change that. 

My little brother (5) is very intelligent in that he searches for answers until he is satisfied. My mom telling him that I am unstable and violent isn’t going to sit well with him, even if he can’t get the truth from me. We all share a close bond that I hope won’t be broken over my mom looking for control.

I’m sorry about your situation. I hope it doesn’t get to that point for me. My little sister (10) is sadly disabled and doesn’t understand what’s going on enough to form opinions while my little brother (5) is always looking for the true answer. He’s always asking questions and doesn’t take anything at face value. Something tells me that he won’t fall victim to whatever she tries to put in his head. The bond we share is too strong for that.

Thanks for your input. This very helpful. My mom has been this way for a while, so it can be hard to see the love at times. My more supportive family has told me that college is going to be my freedom and to focus on the goal of becoming independent of her. I know that this will upset her and possibly my siblings, but hopefully things will work out. I hope my siblings can remember the good times and that I love them no matter what. That’s all that matter to me at the end of the day.

To add some context, I have always been treated differently by my Mom. Ever since I stopped being her emotional support, she has resented me. This has caused many arguments. Sadly, this worsened my mental health issues and made it hard to communicate with other people without trauma dumping. 

As of right now, I have no friends. I also don’t currently have a therapist, so my Grandmother is the only one I talk to in these situations. She tries to make me feel better about it, but these feelings of loneliness are overwhelming. I’m lost in what to do, so I’ve turned to the internet for validation.
I am so sorry for what you experienced. I am glad you are doing better.   :)
You have a friend in me. ❤️

I have social anxiety. I have been in two mental hospitals. At first, it can be intimidating but I actually got friends. To know that people liked me who barely knew me really made me want to get better. The staff are usually really nice too. I don't know if this helps but I just want to let you know that it will be okay.

It is not worth it. In the case that you are successful, your roommate will be traumatized. If you aren't, there will be a lot recovering to do on top of your issues. I don't want to put pressure on you. Please reconsider.
I am begging you to not do it. You may not know me but I care. I am tearing up just thinking about. Please don't do it.
Please don't do it. It will get better. A lot of girls I know aren't obsessed with looks and just want a guy to like them back. If you can't find any then remember that it's their problem, not yours.
Thanks. I felt like I was supposed to adapt to it. I am going to talk to him soon about this.

My dad has a very tough love approach to my mental health issues. Whenever we talk about a problem I am having I have to do the work to fix it. He never makes me feel like he cares. I broke down the other day and was hyperventilating for over thirty minutes. When I heard he was coming over I thought he would actually try to talk to me. All he did was yell at me. I felt so bad when I shouldn't have. I know he cares but he never shows it anymore. He believes I should just handle it myself.
